system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- Evidence text comes from a PDF text layer. If symbols are garbled so that you cannot verify the atom, answer "hold" for that check and say so.
- Be strict. When unsure between pass and a non-pass value, choose the non-pass value and explain.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom. pass = fully stated. revise = the core claim is stated, and the gap is only wording, strength, or a dropped/extra peripheral qualifier that can be fixed by deleting or softening words (say what). fail = not stated, OR the atom adds substantive content the evidence lacks: a scope or population restriction (e.g. 'In B-ALL'), a mechanism or operation, a characterization (e.g. 'an unbounded while loop'), or a formula/definition. If deleting the unsupported part would change what the atom tests, it is fail, not revise. For pass, put the supporting evidence ids in cite (required).
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / revise / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge: one fact a person who studied the concept would simply know. revise = the core fact is recall-level but the sentence carries extra load that must be removed, e.g. stacked conditions (since/although/if ... and ...), a procedural or evaluative add-on ('easy to define but requires checking ...'), or a clause that introduces a second technical concept that must be known separately (e.g. 'if X is an inner Kan complex' when that is not the card concept). fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = the authors' opinion or choice, or the finding of one study, so the answer is not fixed without the source.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a single system, product, or one study's topic.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: Volume kinetics
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Adaptation of pharmacokinetics to infusion fluids using hemodilution, distribution half-lives, fluid efficiency, crystalloid versus colloid time course and effect of hypotension/anesthesia on elimination. Excludes details of tracer dilution methods.

ATOMS:
- IVFLUID-C11-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: Volume kinetics is an elaboration of the hemodilution concept that captures flows of fluid between body fluid compartments over time, and it has similarities to pharmacokinetics.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0119-s15] The hemodilution concept can be elaborated upon to capture flows of fluid between body fluid compartments over time.
    [IVFLUID-p0119-s16] This approach is called volume kinetics and has similarities to pharmacokinetics.
- IVFLUID-C11-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: Volume kinetics differs from conventional pharmacokinetics in that the walls of the body fluid compartments are expandable, and in that its input variable is hemodilution rather than plasma drug concentration.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0119-s17] One important difference is that the walls of the body fluid compartments are expandable [21].
    [IVFLUID-p0119-s18] Another difference is the choice of input variable.
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s01] conventional pharmacokinetics, the plasma concentration of the drug to be studied serves as the input.
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s02] For volume kinetics, hemodilution is used to capture the distribution of the infused water volume.
- IVFLUID-C11-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: Volume kinetics is an adaptation of pharmacokinetic theory that makes it possible to analyze and simulate the distribution and elimination of infusion fluids.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0210-s01] Volume kinetics is an adaptation of pharmacokinetic theory that makes it possible to
    [IVFLUID-p0210-s02] analyze and simulate the distribution and elimination of infusion fluids [35].
- IVFLUID-C11-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: Volume kinetics is based on serial analysis of blood hemoglobin concentration and, at best, urine volume during and after infusion of a fluid in a controlled setting, and blood volume itself is not important to the calculations.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s08] The blood volume is not important to the calculations, but volume kinetics is still based
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s09] on serial analysis of the blood Hb concentration and, at best, the urine volume as well, during and after infusion of a fluid in a controlled setting.
- IVFLUID-C11-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: The rise in blood water concentration after a fluid infusion only seems analogous to a drug concentration in pharmacokinetics, because it represents a dilution of the administered water in a much larger water volume, which adds requirements to the calculations.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s05] The increase in the blood water concentration then seems to yield the same concept as a drug concentration in conventional pharmacokinetics.
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s06] Sadly, though, this is an illusion, because the rise in blood water concentration that occurs when a fluid is infused represents a dilution of administered water in a much larger water volume.
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s07] This fact adds some requirements to the calculations.
- IVFLUID-C11-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: In volume kinetics, hemodilution (decreased blood Hb, hence increased blood water) is used to capture the distribution of the infused water volume, but the rise in blood water concentration is only an apparent analogue of a drug concentration because it represents infused water diluted in a much larger water volume, which adds requirements to the calculations.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s02] For volume kinetics, hemodilution is used to capture the distribution of the infused water volume.
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s03] With regard to volume, the blood contains almost exclusively Hb and water.
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s04] If Hb is decreased, the water component of the blood is increased.
- IVFLUID-C11-S2-04 | S2
  ATOM: By simulation using volume kinetics, one can determine the infusion rate required to reach a predetermined plasma volume expansion.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0210-s03] Applying this concept, it is possible, by simulation, to determine the infusion rate that is required to reach a predetermined plasma volume expansion.
- IVFLUID-C11-S2-05 | S2
  ATOM: Volume kinetic analysis has shown that after expansion by a crystalloid fluid the interstitial fluid space is only twice as large as the plasma volume, which is less than commonly assumed, and crystalloid distribution has a half-life of 8 min.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s10] The results have shown that the interstitial fluid space after expansion by a crystalloid fluid is only twice as large as the plasma volume, i.e., less than commonly assumed.
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s11] The distribution of crystalloid fluid occurs with a half-life of 8 min, except in association with an abrupt drop in arterial pressure, when distribution is temporarily arrested.
- IVFLUID-C11-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: During general anesthesia, elimination of crystalloid fluid is greatly retarded owing to reduced arterial pressure, whereas the intravascular persistence of colloid fluid does not seem to be affected by arterial pressure.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0122-s04] The elimination of crystalloid fluid is greatly retarded during general anesthesia due to
    [IVFLUID-p0122-s05] the reduction in arterial pressure [21].
    [IVFLUID-p0122-s06] By contrast, the intravascular persistence of a colloid fluid does not seem to be affected by the arterial pressure.
- IVFLUID-C11-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: Volume kinetic results show crystalloid distribution occurs with a half-life of 8 min except in association with an abrupt drop in arterial pressure, when distribution is temporarily arrested, so that during such a drop it does not matter whether a crystalloid or a colloid is infused.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s11] The distribution of crystalloid fluid occurs with a half-life of 8 min, except in association with an abrupt drop in arterial pressure, when distribution is temporarily arrested.
    [IVFLUID-p0120-s12] Hence, when the blood pressure drops, it does not matter if one infuses a crystalloid or a colloid fluid.
- IVFLUID-C11-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: The volume kinetic calculations of colloid-versus-crystalloid effectiveness do not assume any injury to the endothelial glycocalyx layer.
  EVIDENCE:
    [IVFLUID-p0122-s08] These calculations do not assume any injury to the endothelial glycocalyx layer.
